findings.title: The R30 TLS-defaults pin checks AsyncClient keyword names, not the transport value, so TLS verification can still be turned off through the allowed transport keyword
findings.evidence: Probe P1_S5b changed `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_HTTP_TIMEOUT, transport=_TRANSPORT)` to `transport=_TRANSPORT or httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(verify=False)`. The whole RED file stayed green: `[pyt] tag=rv-b3b-mut-P1_S5b start=2026-10-17 18:56:41 end=2026-10-17 18:56:46 elapsed=5s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, 106 passed. The reason: R30 only walks calls named AsyncClient and compares their keyword names to {timeout, transport}. The module-level `_TRANSPORT is None` check still holds, and the tests inject a MockTransport, so the transport's own verify=False is never seen. In production that mutant posts the client secret and the refresh token to appleid.apple.com without certificate verification. The shipped code is correct; only the pin is too narrow for what its docstring claims ("production uses httpx's default transport, TLS verified"). The adversary's own S5 shape (verify=False on AsyncClient) is killed by R30.
findings.fix: Tighten R30. Require each AsyncClient's `transport` keyword value to be exactly `ast.Name(id='_TRANSPORT')` and its `timeout` value to be `ast.Name(id='_HTTP_TIMEOUT')`. Also refuse any call in the module, AsyncHTTPTransport included, that carries a verify, trust_env, proxy or proxies keyword.

findings.title: FB5 says the stripped code is what gets exchanged, but only the whitespace-only half is pinned
findings.evidence: Probe P2_X52 kept the stripped gate (`siwa_code = ...strip()` / `if siwa_code:`) but passed `body.authorization_code` instead of `siwa_code` to `store_apple_refresh_token`. The whole RED file stayed green: `[pyt] tag=rv-b3b-mut-P2_X52 start=2026-10-17 18:56:47 end=2026-10-17 18:56:52 elapsed=5s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, 106 passed. If that regression happened, a code with surrounding whitespace would go to Apple unstripped. Apple would answer invalid_grant, logged as `[SIWA] exchange status=400`, nothing would be stored, and that account could never be revoked. The X51 mutant (strip removed) is killed only through R7[whitespace], which tests the whitespace-only case.
findings.fix: Add a padded-code parameter to R6 (or to R7, as a store-expected case), e.g. a code built as "  " + CODE + " \t". Assert that the exchange form's `code` equals the stripped CODE and that exactly one upsert happens.

findings.title: FB4's rule that no key text may appear in an exception is pinned at only one of the two ValueError sites in _normalise_private_key
findings.evidence: Probe P5_S3c changed the second site (`if not decoded.startswith(_PEM_PREFIX): raise ValueError("unparseable private key")`, apple_siwa_service.py:114-115) to append the decoded text. The whole RED file stayed green: `[pyt] tag=rv-b3b-mut-P5_S3c start=2026-10-17 18:57:07 end=2026-10-17 18:57:18 elapsed=11s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, 106 passed. That path runs when the variable holds base64 of ASCII text that does not start with -----BEGIN, for example a .p8 with a leading label line. In that case the decoded text IS key material. R3[garbage] and R9[garbage-key] only reach the first site, because 'garbage-not-a-pem' fails b64decode(validate=True). The effect is bounded: every caller logs only type(exc).__name__. The adversary's S3 shape (the first site) is killed.
findings.fix: Add an R3 parameter with base64 of an ASCII prefix plus the generated PEM. Assert a ValueError and run _assert_no_key_text_in_exception over both functions.
